land.text: Maurice FitzGerald's Desmond lands, which the Crown made an earldom in 1329 and confirmed as the county palatine of Kerry

predecessors.note: The legal predecessor is the Lordship of Ireland under the English Crown (eu-11-x); Cliopatria lists the earldom as a member of the (Kingdom of England) umbrella.

land.text: the Desmond estates 'forfeit to the English Crown' in 1583 and planted with English colonists after a survey begun in 1584

successors.note: The title was recreated in 1600, 1619, 1622 and 1628 for others (page); none of those restores the Geraldine lordship.

capitals.name: Tralee
capitals.note: No page opened names the earls' seat. Tralee is the place of the 1st Earl's burial ('the Friars-preachers church in Tralee') and of the 14th Earl's death ('near Tralee'), in the county palatine of Kerry confirmed to him in 1329. Researcher's reading, low certainty. The infobox seat Newnham Paddox is the modern Denbigh house.

correction.text: the entirety of County Limerick with large parts of Cork, Kerry and Waterford, and the county palatine of Kerry

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1329-1332, which Cliopatria lacks. 'Maurice was created Earl of Desmond by Letters Patent dated at Gloucester, England, 27 August 1329', confirming 'the county palatine of Kerry'; the Earl of Desmond page says the earldom 'historically comprised what is now the entirety of County Limerick, with large parts of Cork, Kerry, and Waterford' (undated). The four counties are the researcher's reading of that sentence; 16,900 km2 on the grid.

correction.text: the entirety of County Limerick with large parts of Cork, Kerry and Waterford

keyframe_review.note: 2,376 km2 on seven grid cells at 54.36-54.86N, 5.65-6.09W: the County Antrim and Down coast around Carrickfergus, cell for cell the Cliopatria Earldom of Ulster shape of 1326-1332. The Earl of Desmond page puts the earldom in Limerick, Cork, Kerry and Waterford (Munster), and the Earldom of Ulster page (capital Carrickfergus, most of Antrim and Down) puts this land in Ulster. A row mix-up in Cliopatria; the shape is replaced by the Desmond lands. The 1st Earl's imprisonment in 1331 and the 1345 revolt do not change this.

12,998 km2: 43 Munster cells covering Kerry (9), Cork (13), Limerick (10) and Waterford (6) plus five cells of South Tipperary and single cells in Kilkenny and Wexford; against the four counties of the page (about 16,900 km2) this is the 'large parts' the page describes. The page dates no change in 1352 (the 1st Earl died on 25 January 1356 and the 3rd Earl Gerald succeeded in 1358 or 1359, the Gerald page's infobox and text disagreeing), so the date is Cliopatria's. Reviewer eu-11-j changed the verdict from ok to adjust: every other keyframe 1329-1583 is the four-county union, so an ok here made the drawn shape shrink in 1352 and grow back in 1385 with no ledger event.

correction.text: the Desmond lands of Limerick, Cork, Kerry and Waterford, as in the 1329-1351 and 1385-1583 keyframes; no page opened gives the earls the South Tipperary, Kilkenny or Wexford cells
the Desmond lands of Limerick, Cork, Kerry and Waterford; no page opened gives the earls any land in Wexford

keyframe_review.note: 14,800 km2: the same Munster core plus seven cells of County Wexford and one each of Carlow and Kilkenny. The Gerald FitzGerald page, the only page that touches 1359-1398, has the 3rd Earl as Lord Chief Justice in 1367, beaten by Brian O'Brien of Thomond at Limerick in 1370 ('burning the city and Desmond's lands') and gone by 1398, and records no Leinster land. Corrected to the page's four counties.

correction.text: Limerick, Cork, Kerry and Waterford; the Tipperary, Kilkenny, Laois and Kildare cells lie outside the four counties the page names

keyframe_review.note: 20,188 km2, the shape's maximum: it adds the two Tipperary districts (18 cells), Kilkenny (7), Laois (5), Kildare (4) and Wexford to the Munster core. None of it lies in the four counties the page names; the page says the earldom 'bordered the Kingdom of Desmond, the Kingdom of Thomond, and the Earldom of Ormond', but where Ormond lay is on no page opened (the Earl of Ormond page is only a disambiguation page). No page gives Desmond that land. Corrected to the four counties; the 20,188 km2 is 20% above the four counties' 16,900.

correction.text: the entirety of County Limerick with large parts of Cork, Kerry and Waterford

keyframe_review.note: 6,858 km2 on 28 cells in North and South Tipperary (13), Kilkenny (6), Laois (6) and one cell each in Limerick, Waterford, Offaly and Wexford: almost none of the Desmond core. The page's Limerick, Cork, Kerry and Waterford are absent, so the shape cannot be the earldom (0 of its Kerry and Cork cells). The 5th and 6th Earls (died 1420 and 1463 on the page) leave no event for a collapse in 1422. Replaced by the four counties.

correction.text: the entirety of County Limerick with large parts of Cork, Kerry and Waterford

keyframe_review.note: Identical 6,858 km2 Tipperary-Kilkenny-Laois shape for 1453-1458 as 1422; same verdict. Cliopatria ends its row in 1458; the earldom itself lasts to 1583 ('held by his descendants until 1583').

correction.text: the Desmond lands held until the forfeiture of 1583

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1459-1583, which Cliopatria lacks: the page says the Desmond line 'held it until 1583 when they rose against the English crown', and the 14th Earl was killed that year. The Desmond Rebellions page puts the fighting in 'the Province of Munster'. Extent is the same four counties (page undated); the western half of Desmond proper 'lived on as a semi-independent Gaelic kingdom until 1596' beside it.

region.text: the county palatine of Kerry and the Desmond lands

ledger.note: 1329: Edward III makes Maurice FitzGerald Earl of Desmond (27 August). 'Maurice was created Earl of Desmond by Letters Patent dated at Gloucester, England, 27 August 1329', confirming 'the county palatine of Kerry' to him and his heirs male, held of the Crown by one knight's fee. The extent is the Earl of Desmond page's undated description (Limerick, Cork, Kerry, Waterford).

region.text: Dunamark, at the head of Bantry Bay

ledger.note: 1331: the Crown takes Dunamark, at the head of Bantry Bay. The Crown imprisoned him in 1331 for over 18 months over the rumours of a plot to make him King of Ireland; 'An inquisition then declared Dunamark, at the head of Bantry Bay, to be Crown property, reducing his estates.' The inquisition's own year is not given.

1579: the Earl joins the Second Desmond Rebellion by sacking Youghal (13 November). James FitzMaurice landed at Smerwick near Dingle on 18 July 1579 and was killed on 18 August; the Earl 'joined the rebellion by sacking Youghal (on 13 November)'.

1583: the Earl is hunted down and killed. 'On 2 November 1583 the earl was hunted down and killed near Tralee in Kerry' (Desmond Rebellions); the Earl of Desmond page gives 11 November 1583. The rising had been crushed by mid-1581; 30,000 had died of hunger by April 1582.

1583: the Desmond earldom is forfeit. 'The 14th Earl was defeated and killed by forces loyal to Queen Elizabeth I on 11 November 1583. His title, along with the enormous estates of his family, were forfeit to the English Crown'; after a survey begun in 1584 the Munster lands were planted with English colonists (Desmond Rebellions).

wars.name: Desmond's revolt of 1345
wars.outcome: The 1st Earl presided at an assembly at Callan in 1345, ignored a summons, attacked Nenagh, surrendered on a promise of his life, was imprisoned and lost his lands; released in 1348 and pardoned in 1349. No territorial change is recorded.
wars.note: The page does not date the surrender or say what became of his lands; not drawn.

wars.name: Desmond-Thomond war of 1370
wars.outcome: 'In 1370 Brian O'Brien of Thomond expelled his cousin Turlough. Brian marched on Limerick, and defeated Desmond, burning the city and Desmond's lands and imprisoning him.'

wars.name: First Desmond Rebellion
wars.outcome: English victory: James FitzMaurice attacked the English colony at Kerrycurihy in June 1569, Donal MacCarthy Mor surrendered in November 1569, and FitzMaurice submitted on 23 February 1573.
wars.note: The rebellion was led by the Earl's cousin FitzMaurice, not the Earl himself (page: infobox 'June 1569 - 23 February 1573').

wars.name: Second Desmond Rebellion

zones.text: the rising spread to Leinster in July 1580; the English were destroyed at Glenmalure on 25 August 1580

wars.outcome: English victory: Smerwick 18 July 1579, Youghal sacked 13 November 1579, papal troops landed at Smerwick 10 September 1580, the rebellion crushed by mid-1581, the Earl killed in November 1583; the estates are forfeit and planted.

certainty.note: A feudal earldom with no survey: the page describes its land only as 'historically' Limerick, Cork, Kerry and Waterford, and the western part was a semi-independent Gaelic kingdom to 1596. The county palatine of Kerry (1329) is the one legal unit.

notes:
Written by eu-11-j on 2026-10-25 from five pages (budget 5; one of them, 'Earl of Ormond', was a disambiguation page and gave nothing). The pages are thin on territory: they describe the earldom as 'historically' Limerick, Cork, Kerry and Waterford and give almost no dates for gains and losses.

CLIOPATRIA PROBLEMS (all keyframes): the 1333-1351 shape is the Earldom of Ulster's shape (Antrim and Down, seven identical cells), a row mix-up: verdict 'wrong'. The 1352-1384 shape is the Munster core and is 'ok'. The 1385-1394 and 1395-1421 shapes add Wexford, Tipperary, Kilkenny, Laois and Kildare: 'adjust' to the page's four counties. The 1422-1458 shape lies in Tipperary, Kilkenny and Laois and has almost none of the core: 'wrong'. Cliopatria ends the row in 1458, but the earldom lasted to 1583 (page), so the dossier ends in November 1583 and has new keyframes for 1329-1332 and 1459-1583. All corrections are the same four-county union, so a gap-filler who opens 'Gaelic resurgence', 'Lordship of Ireland' or the 4th-7th Earls could add the real shrinkage and growth (the 6th Earl 'the Usurper', the 7th Earl's death in 1468 are on the page only as dates of death).

OVERLAP WARNING: Cliopatria's Kingdom of England row (1333-1458, 'Kingdom of England' shapes on Ireland) overlaps this dossier's four counties. The earldom is a member of the (Kingdom of England) umbrella; rule 4 would draw it as a lighter tint of England's colour (type 'state' kept; a vassal_start in the england dossier would do it). The renderers or the England dossier should decide.

Not recorded: the 1345 forfeiture of lands (page gives imprisonment and loss of lands, no year or extent), the 1600-1601 restoration of the Tower Earl and the second to fourth creations (1600, 1619, 1622/1628, others' titles).
Pages disagree: the Earl's death is 2 November 1583 (Desmond Rebellions) or 11 November 1583 (Earl of Desmond); month 11 used for both. The Earl of Desmond page also gives the first creation's extinction as 1582 (infobox) and 1583 (text).
Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-england (the Crown; a Lordship of Ireland is eu-11-x), Thomond (O'Brien) and the MacCarthy Mor kingdom of Desmond (Gaelic polities; not Cliopatria rows; the page says western Desmond lived on 'until 1596').
Gazetteer: Dunamark/Bantry (used lon/lat), Askeaton, Youghal, Kinsale and Nenagh are not in places.jsonl; a 'Thomond' region is missing; 'Desmond' as a region would help.
